events.title: Pepin the Short dies, leaving the Franks to Charlemagne and Carloman
events.description: King Pepin died at Saint-Denis, dividing his kingdom between his sons Charles and Carloman, who were crowned in October. After Carloman's death in 771, Charlemagne ruled alone.
events.html: King Pepin died at Saint-Denis, dividing his kingdom between his sons Charles and Carloman, who were crowned in October. After Carloman's death in 771, Charlemagne ruled alone.

events.title: The Second Council of Nicaea opens
events.description: The Second Council of Nicaea opened in the church of Hagia Sophia at Nicaea, the site of the first ecumenical council. About 350 members attended under the presidency of Tarasios, and 308 bishops or their representatives signed its acts.
events.html: The Second Council of Nicaea opened in the church of Hagia Sophia at Nicaea, the site of the first ecumenical council. About 350 members attended under the presidency of Tarasios, and 308 bishops or their representatives signed its acts.

events.title: Basil I has Emperor Michael III assassinated
events.description: Basil I, a peasant's son whom Michael III had made co-emperor the year before, had Michael assassinated in his chamber and became sole ruler. He founded the Macedonian dynasty, which ruled for nearly two centuries.
events.html: Basil I, a peasant's son whom Michael III had made co-emperor the year before, had Michael assassinated in his chamber and became sole ruler. He founded the Macedonian dynasty, which ruled for nearly two centuries.

events.title: Parliamentarians defeat Charles I at the Battle of Rowton Heath
events.description: Parliamentarian forces under Sydnam Poyntz inflicted a significant defeat on the Royalists under the personal command of King Charles I, with heavy losses, preventing him from relieving the siege of Chester.
events.html: Parliamentarian forces under Sydnam Poyntz inflicted a significant defeat on the Royalists under the personal command of King Charles I, with heavy losses, preventing him from relieving the siege of Chester.

events.title: Washington signs the Judiciary Act
events.description: The Judiciary Act set up the federal court system, fixed the Supreme Court at six justices and created the office of Attorney General. It remains the foundation of the US federal judiciary.
events.html: The Judiciary Act set up the federal court system, fixed the Supreme Court at six justices and created the office of Attorney General. It remains the foundation of the US federal judiciary.

events.title: Gold price collapses on 'Black Friday'
events.description: Jay Gould and James Fisk's attempt to corner the gold market collapsed when the Grant administration sold Treasury gold. Prices crashed and many speculators were ruined.
events.html: Jay Gould and James Fisk's attempt to corner the gold market collapsed when the Grant administration sold Treasury gold. Prices crashed and many speculators were ruined.

events.title: B. R. Ambedkar and Hindu leaders sign the Poona Pact
events.description: Agreed with Gandhi during his fast, the Poona Pact was signed, replacing separate electorates for the 'depressed classes' with reserved seats. Gandhi ended his fast against separate electorates two days later.
events.html: Agreed with Gandhi during his fast, the Poona Pact was signed, replacing separate electorates for the 'depressed classes' with reserved seats. Gandhi ended his fast against separate electorates two days later.

events.title: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty opens for signature
events.description: The CTBT, banning all nuclear explosions, opened for signature at the UN and was signed first by President Clinton. It has not entered into force, as key states have not ratified it.
events.html: The CTBT, banning all nuclear explosions, opened for signature at the UN and was signed first by President Clinton. It has not entered into force, as key states have not ratified it.
